question: Explain in brief about Flow Layout.
answerMd:
### GUI Layout Managers in Java: FlowLayout, BorderLayout & GridLayout

A **LayoutManager** is an interface that automatically governs the positioning, sizing, and responsive reflow of GUI components within a container.

| Layout Manager | Organization Principle | Default Component Sizing |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`FlowLayout`** | Arranges components in a directional row (like words on a line); wraps to next row if container shrinks. | Retains **preferred size**. |
| **`BorderLayout`** | Divides container into **5 regions**: `NORTH`, `SOUTH`, `EAST`, `WEST`, and `CENTER`. | Expands components to fill regional boundaries. |
| **`GridLayout`** | Divides container into a 2D rectangular grid of **equal-sized rows and columns**. | All components are forced to **identical width and height**. |

$$\therefore \text{Layout managers ensure responsive GUI layouts that adapt gracefully across window resizing events.}$$
